issue_03_common_support_lomfo.question: Do the A-vs-C and B-vs-C regime-utility comparisons change once A and B are scored on exactly the same 396-row common support that C (LOMFO) actually covers, instead of A/B's full 449-row support?
issue_03_common_support_lomfo.motivation: LOMFO (regime C) only ever holds out rows belonging to one of the 9 'major' families (n>=15), so only 396 of 449 dev-population rows are ever scored as an LOMFO test row; A and B score all 449. Comparing A/B's 449-row MAE against C's 396-row MAE conflates a support-size difference with a regime-design difference.
issue_03_common_support_lomfo.method: Reproduce regime A and B's exact fold partitions from artifacts/npj_n4b_nested_internal_validation.json (same CV_SEED=20260921, same random_kfold_splits/family_group_kfold_splits functions). For each of the 8 models, refit each fold using that fold's ALREADY-FROZEN per_fold_hyperparameters (no new tuning) via fit_predict_model, producing full 449-row OOF predictions. Sanity-check: recomputed pooled MAE over all 449 rows must match the frozen n4b pooled_mae within 1e-6 before trusting any subset number. Then restrict both A's and B's OOF predictions to the 396-row common-support mask (family_filled isin n4b's major_families list) and recompute pooled MAE per model. C's existing pooled_mae_over_major_family_rows is already on this exact support and is reused unchanged. Feed the three regimes' common-support internal-MAE dicts into the SAME regime_summary/bootstrap_regime_pair_delta_ci functions N7b used, against the same frozen N6 external residuals.
issue_03_common_support_lomfo.decision_rule: Report median |MAE gap|, Spearman rho, Kendall tau, and regret for A/B/C on the common 396-row support, with bootstrap CIs, and compare directly to N7b's full-support numbers. No claim of a changed verdict unless a CI crosses the sign the full-support comparison found.

issue_04_training_size_matched_control.question: Is the extreme MAE degradation some models (ridge, shallow_mlp) show under Family-GroupKFold (regime B) attributable to training-size loss alone, independent of which rows/family were excluded?
issue_04_training_size_matched_control.motivation: Regime B's fold 0 removes a large family from training (up to ~213/449 rows across its 5 folds' varying sizes), confounding family-novelty with a large training-size reduction.
issue_04_training_size_matched_control.method: For each of regime B's 5 folds (fixed sizes, from family_group_kfold_splits(seed=20260921)), construct a plain random row-level holdout of the IDENTICAL test-set size (sse_transfer.evaluation.npj_internal_validation.size_matched_random_splits), for 3 deterministic control seeds (20260930, 20260931, 20260932). For each (seed, fold, model), run the identical nested tuning pipeline used by N4b (inner-split tune_hyperparameters on that fold's own outer-train partition, then fit_predict_model) -- full nested retuning, not a reuse of B's hyperparameters, so the matched control is judged under the same protocol as the reference regime. Compute pooled MAE per model per seed. Compare against B's actual per-model pooled MAE (from n4b) and A's (random CV) pooled MAE.
issue_04_training_size_matched_control.scope_decision: Matched-size controls are built for regime B (Family-GroupKFold) only, not regime C (LOMFO), to bound compute to the ~2.5-3h budget agreed with the author. This is a disclosed scope reduction, not a claim that LOMFO's blowups are unexamined by any means (N4b/N15 already diagnose LOMFO's family-exclusion mechanism qualitatively).
issue_04_training_size_matched_control.decision_rule: If a model's matched-size-random pooled MAE is within the same order of magnitude as regime A (random CV) and far below regime B's actual blowup MAE, the degradation is attributable to family-exclusion distribution shift, not size loss alone. If the matched-size-random control ALSO blows up to a similar magnitude as regime B, size loss alone is sufficient to explain it. No causal claim beyond what the comparison directly shows.

issue_05_fold_local_robust_shift_distanc.question: Does N21e's 'robust' shift-distance fix (artifacts/npj_n21e_robust_shift_distance.json) actually avoid inspecting outer-test features, or does its normalization still reference full-449-population variance?
issue_05_fold_local_robust_shift_distanc.motivation: N21e's near-zero-variance threshold was computed as 5% of the FULL 449-row population's per-feature variance. A fold-local diagnostic must be normalized using ONLY that fold's own training features (or an independently frozen threshold), never any statistic of the pooled population that includes the outer-test rows.
issue_05_fold_local_robust_shift_distanc.method: Audit n21e_robust_shift_distance.py's variance-threshold computation directly (read the code, do not assume). Rebuild the same NN-distance/Wasserstein diagnostic so that, for every outer fold, the near-zero-variance threshold and any standardization scale are computed from that fold's OWN training partition only, matching regime A/B/C's actual fold structure (this necessarily produces one threshold per fold per regime, not one global threshold). No target labels are used at any point (target-free diagnostic, as N15/N21e already were).
issue_05_fold_local_robust_shift_distanc.decision_rule: Report old (population-normalized) vs corrected (fold-local-normalized) max/median/q90 standardized distance per regime, and state explicitly whether the conclusion that regime B's excluded family sits far outside its fold's training distribution survives the fold-local correction.

issue_06_doi_cluster_bootstrap.question: Does accounting for multiple Hargreaves compositions sharing a literature source (DOI) widen the external-MAE bootstrap CIs beyond the existing row-level bootstrap?
issue_06_doi_cluster_bootstrap.motivation: Row-level bootstrap (used throughout N7b/N15) treats every one of the 204 strict-cohort compositions as independent, but compositions from the same paper may be correlated (shared synthesis batch, shared measurement protocol/equipment).
issue_06_doi_cluster_bootstrap.method: For each of the 204 strict-cohort reduced_formula rows, look up its contributing raw rows' 'source' (DOI) values from data/processed/npj_external_cohort/hargreaves_overlap_ledger.csv (RETAINED rows only). Build source-sharing clusters via union-find (formulas sharing >=1 DOI join the same cluster; a formula with a single unique DOI not shared by any other retained formula is its own singleton cluster). Resample CLUSTERS (not rows) with replacement, reconstructing a bootstrap sample's row set as the union of all rows in the resampled clusters, for each of N6's frozen per-model residuals. Recompute external MAE bootstrap CIs and, reusing bootstrap_regime_pair_delta_ci's statistic definitions, the primary A-vs-B/A-vs-C regime-utility deltas under cluster resampling.
issue_06_doi_cluster_bootstrap.decision_rule: Report cluster count, cluster-size distribution, and side-by-side row-bootstrap vs cluster-bootstrap CI widths/point estimates for external MAE and the primary regime-utility deltas. Flag explicitly if any conclusion's CI sign flips under cluster resampling.

issue_08b_chemical_system_cluster_contro.question: Beyond the existing exact-formula-disjoint control (N20b), does grouping by chemical system (element set, ignoring stoichiometry) -- a strictly coarser, more conservative grouping -- change internal-CV MAE materially?
issue_08b_chemical_system_cluster_contro.motivation: N20b's formula-GroupKFold groups only EXACT-duplicate reduced formulas; it does not address near-duplicate chemical redundancy (e.g. two different stoichiometries of the same element set).
issue_08b_chemical_system_cluster_contro.feasibility_check: Valid only if grouping by element-set does not collapse most of the dev population into one or two enormous groups (which would make the regime degenerate, not a meaningful control). Computed and disclosed before running the full nested pipeline.
issue_08b_chemical_system_cluster_contro.method: Define chemical_system(formula) = frozenset of elements in the pymatgen-parsed composition (ignoring stoichiometric amounts). GroupKFold on this key, otherwise identical protocol to N20b (same nested tuning pipeline, same seed, same model ladder).
issue_08b_chemical_system_cluster_contro.decision_rule: If the feasibility check fails (degenerate group sizes), report why and do not run the nested pipeline -- document as 'not valid' per the task's own instruction, keeping only the exact-formula control. If valid, report pooled MAE per model vs N4b random-5fold and vs N20b formula-GroupKFold.
